- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.3), model underestimates; adjust downward by 3–7% to avoid missing downside.
- Model often overshoots after sharp upward spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3–5 days); cap forecast at 1.5x recent high for 3–7 day horizon.
- Mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is > 1.2x 18d average, reduce by 10–15% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- For 30d horizon, if sentiment is mixed or neutral (±0.2), model tends to overfit recent volatility; smooth forecast by 1–2% downward.
- If sentiment history shows repeated reversal (e.g., +0.6 → -0.4 → +0.5), model fails to anticipate; reduce forecast by 5–8% for next 5–10 days.
